stops.title: Vector & Cartesian equations of a line; distance of point/skew lines
stops.inShort: Line through a parallel to b: r = a + λ b; Cartesian: (x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = (z − z₁)/c. Shortest distance between skew lines r = a₁ + λb₁ and r = a₂ + μb₂: d = |(a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂)| / |b₁ × b₂|.
sections: 6.1 Vector & Cartesian Equations of a Line
6.2 Distance of a Point from a Line

stops.title: Equations of a plane & angle/distance
stops.inShort: Normal form: r · n̂ = p; passing through a with normal n: r · n = a · n (Cartesian: ax + by + cz = d). Distance of point r₁ from r·n = d: |r₁·n − d| / |n|.
sections: 6.7 Distance of a Point from a Plane

items.f: r = a + λ b,  d_skew = |(a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂)| / |b₁ × b₂|
r · n = a · n,  d = |ax₁ + by₁ + cz₁ − d₀| / √(a² + b² + c²)
items.s: Angle between line (dir b) & plane (normal n): sin θ = |b·n|/(|b||n|).

board.text: The vector equation of the line passing through the point having position vector 4i − j + 2k and parallel to vector −2i − j + k is given by ____.
board.answer: (d) (4i − j + 2k) + λ(−2i − j + k) (using r = a + λb).

points.text: Correct option: (d) (4i − j + 2k) + λ(−2i − j + k)

board.text: Equation of line passing through the points (0, 0, 0) and (2, 1, −3) is ____.
Find the vector and Cartesian equations of the plane passing through the points A(1, 1, −2), B(1, 2, 1) and C(2, −1, 1).
board.answer:
AB = (0, 1, 3), AC = (1, −2, 3).
Normal n = AB × AC = |i j k; 0 1 3; 1 −2 3| = 9i + 3j − k.
Vector equation: r · (9i + 3j − k) = (i + j − 2k) · (9i + 3j − k) = 9 + 3 + 2 = 14.
Cartesian equation: 9x + 3y − z = 14.

points.text: Vectors AB, AC and normal n = AB × AC = 9i + 3j − k
